chunks: From him, from Safwan and Ali ibn al-Nu'man and Uthman ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

My father sent me with a bag containing one thousand dirhams to a money-changer from the people of Iraq, and he ordered me to tell him: 'Sell them (the dirhams). When you have sold them, take their price and buy for us Madani dirhams with that price.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging currency of different types or origins in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that his father, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir, sent him to exchange a bag of dirhams with a money-changer in Iraq, instructing him to sell the original currency and purchase Madani dirhams with the proceeds. This hadith, found in the chapter on exchanging one coin for two or more, illustrates the permissibility of currency exchange (sarf) involving different regional standards, highlighting the practical economic jurisprudence of the Ahl al-Bayt in managing trade and monetary value.
